result.unit: ch5b tail: the honest part and verdict (825.00-875.39)
result.summary: Clean, well-synced range. A frame-difference scan of all 1512 frames found no render glitches, no unintended black frames and no single-frame flashes. The only full-frame flash is the planned shutter at 870.80. All 15 marker events land within 0.15 s of their words (gh, agul, needles, compass, north2, coin2, likely, v_ant, single, dots, lopside, northl, avoid2, force, snap). The truck, compass-settles-on-north and JUICE CHECK stamp gags all read, and every on-screen text matches the locked script. There are four majors, all cheap parameter fixes. (1) At 'tore apart around Antarctica' the ringed Antarctica, where the scars converge, is cut off by the bottom edge, and the South America scar runs along the bottom 5 %. I rebuilt the engine camera model from globe.js; it matches the render within about 5 px, and I used it to compute a corrected camera. (2) The Cape Agulhas tip marker on the ASTER photo sits in the bottom 12 % for the whole 5.6 s shot. (3) Slice, then a 1.1 s antipode-map flash, then the same slice again: the slice arrives 2.7 s early under 'the land that avoids land?'. (4) The Polaroid verdict is frozen for 3.6 s at the end of the chapter. Minors: the edge-on coin reads as a signpost under the stamp; the Good Hope to Agulhas comparison is complete for only 0.19 s before the cut; the Polaroid photo is a tight crop of Africa rather than the whole drip globe. Evidence frames are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/ and the scan and projection scripts are in .../y2_ch5b_tail/scripts/.

issues.problem: At the key line 'scars from a supercontinent that tore apart around Antarctica' the camera is centred on the Agulhas tip (lat -33..-36). The scars therefore converge on a ringed Antarctica that sits at the very bottom of the frame: the -68 deg ring runs off the bottom edge with Antarctica cut, and the South America scar is a short squiggle along the bottom edge. The planned 'scar lines glow on South America, Africa and India' reads as two lines running off the bottom of the frame.
issues.evidence: Exact frame /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_853.90.jpg: Africa scar ends at (760,965), South America scar at y~1015-1030, yellow ring spans y~870-1080 and is clipped. I rebuilt the camera model from lib/globe.js set()/project() and lib/shots.js camAt(). With the N2 keys it reproduces the render within ~5 px: Agulhas (935,533), Cape Horn (734,1022), Kanyakumari (1344,163), South Pole (1099,1026), ring y 870-1081, cape_horn track ymax 1036.
issues.fix: ch5b.js, N2 shot (line ~800): keys -> [{ t: N2a, lat: -55, lon: 15, alt: 3.2, heading: 8 }, { t: N2b, lat: -58, lon: 12, alt: 3.1, heading: 8 }]. Computed with the same model (drift 0.6): Agulhas tip at y~320-350, Cape Horn ~(695,790), South Pole y~825-835, -68 deg ring y 633-944 (whole ring in frame and above the 12 % line), and all three scar polylines in frame (cape_horn ymax <= 800). Confirm with one still at 853.9.

issues.problem: The red marker on the real tip of Africa, the focal point of 'REAL TIP: CAPE AGULHAS', sits in the bottom-12 % band for the entire ASTER shot (y 977 -> 951 px, 90 -> 88 %). Captions or the player bar would cover it, and the subject is jammed against the bottom edge. Cause: the tip is at 0.908 of the 1920x1037 plate and the Ken Burns crop is clamped to the plate's bottom edge, so py = (1 - 0.092*z)*H. Getting the tip above the band would need z >= 2.2, which is too soft on this plate.
issues.evidence: Exact frame /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_834.00.jpg: tip dot at (885,962) and ring down to y~992. The M2 crop math gives py = 976.7 at u=0 and 950.8 at u=1. The ASTER plate measures 1920x1037.
issues.fix: ch5b.js, M2 ASTER scene (lines ~737-746). Compute the crop (sx, sw, already computed for the marker) first. Then draw the plate 130 px higher: F.kenburns(ctx, aster, u, 0, -130, W, H, {from: KBf, to: KBt, grade: 'cold'}). Extend the sea into the vacated band: ctx.drawImage(aster, sx, ih - 2, sw, 2, 0, H - 130, W, 130); F.grade(ctx, 0, H - 130, W, 130, 'cold'). Add a ~120 px rgba(5,10,20,0->0.35) gradient over the join, and draw the marker at py - 130. The tip then sits at 847 -> 821 px (78 -> 76 %).

issues.problem: The order goes slice, then map, then slice again (A-B-A), with three cuts in 3.3 s. The equatorial-slice disc cuts in on 'north,' and sits under 'the land that avoids land?', where it has nothing to do with the line. Then a 1.1 s antipode-map flash interrupts it, too short to parse as a callback. Then the identical slice returns for 'There's no clear sign of a deep force'. The narration order is north-land, then antipodes, then deep force, and the visuals do not follow it. The script's visual note says antipode glimpse, then slice, but its marker cue puts the slice at {m:northl}; the build followed both.
issues.evidence: Exact frames /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_863.80.jpg (slice on screen while 'the land that avoids' is spoken) and .../ex/x_865.60.jpg (antipode map). The frame-diff scan shows hard cuts at 863.07, 865.20 and 866.33. In the code: O1b = M.northl - 0.08, O2b = M.avoid2 - 0.07, O3b = M.avoid2 + 1.05.
issues.fix: ch5b.js, O1/O2 section (lines ~838-883). Set O1b = M.northl + 0.66 so the north-land globe holds through 'piled up in the north,'. Show the antipode Equal Earth map as scene(O1b, M.avoid2 + 0.5) (~863.83-865.79, about 2 s, under 'the land that avoids land?'). Start the slice at M.avoid2 + 0.5 with drawSlice(ctx, t, M.avoid2 + 0.5) so the disc grows in on 'There's no clear sign...'. Delete the first scene(O2a, O2b, drawSlice...). The arrow and X stay keyed to M.force, so the arrow lands ~1.7 s after the disc.

issues.problem: Once the caption wipe completes, the Polaroid verdict card is effectively frozen for 3.6 s until the module ends. It holds over 'of where the drifting pieces happen to be right now' and the 0.9 s pause. The scripted drift is only +2 % scale and +0.6 deg of rotation over 4.6 s, which is imperceptible.
issues.evidence: Exact frames /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_873.80.jpg and .../ex/x_875.30.jpg are near-identical. The frame-diff scan gives 871.77-875.37 a mean per-frame diff of 0.11, against ~0.2 for the slowest 'gentle life' globe shots. In the code: bz = lerp(1.25, 1.32, u), rotate + 0.01*u, scale * (1 + 0.02*u).
issues.fix: ch5b.js, P scene (lines ~905-909): bz = lerp(1.25, 1.5, u); ctx.rotate(lerp(-0.09, -0.035, ip) + 0.035 * u); sc = lerp(1.08, 1.0, ip) * (1 + 0.08 * u). That gives a visible slow push (about 8 % and 2 deg) through the closing line and the pause into the ch6 card.

issues.problem: The callback coin stops dead edge-on directly under the JUICE CHECK stamp. There is no surface and no shadow, so it reads as a gold post holding up the 'IT'S COMPLICATED' sign rather than 'the coin landed on its edge'.
issues.evidence: Exact frame /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_849.60.jpg: a ~30 px wide gold bar at x=960, y 480-800, centred 70 px under the stamp.
issues.fix: ch5b.js, N1 extra (lines ~789-790). Add a soft contact shadow once the coin lands: ctx.ellipse(960, 806, 100, 12, ...) at alpha 0.45 from M.likely - 0.2. Use a bigger decaying balance wobble: lean = 0.16 * Math.exp(-1.5 * (t - M.likely)) * Math.sin((t - M.likely) * 6). Move the stamp off the coin's axis: U.drawStamp(ctx, stampC, 1230, 290, ...).

issues.problem: The Good Hope to Agulhas comparison (white dot, dashed hop, red dot, latitude line showing Agulhas is farther south) is complete for only 0.19 s before the hard cut to the ASTER photo. The 'farther south' proof barely registers.
issues.evidence: Exact frame /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_830.95.jpg shows the complete state 0.07 s before the cut. In the code the hop runs M.gh+0.25 -> +0.95 (done at 830.68), the latitude line runs M.gh+0.35 -> +1.1 (done at 830.83), and LMb = M.agul - 0.07 = 831.02.
issues.fix: ch5b.js, LM extra (lines ~723-725): hp = prog(t, M.gh + 0.05, M.gh + 0.6, E.inOut) and lp = prog(t, M.gh + 0.15, M.gh + 0.7, E.inOut). The comparison is then complete by ~830.43 and readable for ~0.6 s before the cut.

issues.problem: The Polaroid 'snapshot' should be the s001 drip globe. Instead it shows a tight crop: southern Africa and Madagascar in orange on dark ocean, the globe's edge only in a corner, and South America, India and the South Pole ring outside the photo. 'A snapshot of where the drifting pieces happen to be' reads as a dark close-up of Africa rather than a photo of the planet.
issues.evidence: Exact frame /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y2_ch5b_tail/ex/x_873.80.jpg. getSnap renders at alt 2.35, a disc radius of ~553 px, but the photo shows only an 840 px window around the screen centre.
issues.fix: ch5b.js, getSnap (line ~894): api.drawGlobe(tc, { lat: -30, lon: 20, alt: 3.6, tilt: 0, heading: 0 }, ...). The disc radius becomes ~393 px, which fits the 840 px crop, so the whole drip globe shows in the photo: the globe's edge, South America, India, and the South Pole ring at y~913.

result.unit: ch5 where the drips are pointing, part 1 (10:04-11:15), 604.37-675.00 s, module ch5a (s072-s079 start)
result.summary:
Pacing and sync are strong in this unit. There is a cut or mode change every 4-6 s. The 10 fps motion scan found no static hold over 3 s, no black frames and no stray flashes; the only luma spikes are the intended flashes at the Gondwana lock (617.05) and the India slam (670.25). Almost every planned beat lands on its marker word:
- The four continent fills land on r_sam 609.87, r_afr 611.07, r_ind 611.87 and r_aus 612.59.
- The lock flash, shake and GONDWANA title land on gond 616.97. The Antarctica ring lands on ant 619.61, and the KEYPIECE pill and lift-drop on "keypiece".
- The Bacon insert lands on remember 623.55. Its Ken Burns zoom works and the quote pill pops on "Is".
- The cut back to the globe lands on point 628.91, and the three drip arrows converge on the ring at whole 629.55.
- The cracks land on "Cracks" 634.31, and the cyan Africa/Antarctica rift on afant 637.67.
- The split glow lands on 643.09, the seam glow on 648.29 and the snap burst on snap2 651.65.
- In the Explorer gag, the wave lands on leave 654.19, the ring and pill on stay 655.47 and the porch light on house 658.91.
- The India streak lands on sprint 660.19, the crawl trails on afaus 664.75, the siren and motion lines on driving 668.59, and the shock rings and flash on slam 670.19.
- The paper figure's counter jumps 38 to 180 on "explanation".

One systemic map defect stops this unit from shipping. Several continents are only partly part of the tracked plates that get highlighted:
- South America has no southern cone (the drip itself).
- Africa has no north-east quarter or Horn.

These parts render as plain sand, behind a straight cut edge. In the paper figure they are missing completely. This shows on the name beats, the Gondwana lock, the drip-arrow proof, the unzip and the textbook figure.

There is also one major sync issue: the zipper pull appears about 1.75 s after its marker. Two minor polish items are listed below.

Chunks 45 onward are not rendered yet, so nothing after 675 s was checked. Evidence files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/y1_ch5a/ (g/crop_610.40.jpg, g/crop_617.40.jpg, g/c_bacon.jpg, z/zip_strip.jpg, g/crop_656.80.jpg, g/crop_674.00.jpg, scan10.txt).

issues.segment: s072-s079 (name fills, Gondwana, keypiece, drip arrows, unzip, everyone moves out, India, paper figure)
issues.problem: On "South America" only a square northern block (cut by a straight white edge at about 28.5°S, sitting on the globe's left limb) and a tiny detached Patagonian tip turn orange. The whole southern cone stays sand-coloured, and that cone is the drip the video is about. Africa likewise lacks its north-east quarter and the Horn, which stay sand, with a stray orange Sinai speck inside them. In the 180 Ma paper textbook figure (from 672.35) the cone is not drawn at all: South America becomes a flat-bottomed block plus a floating blob, and Africa has a notch missing. The Cape Horn drip arrow (629.55) fires from a speck beside a big unhighlighted cone, so the key proof does not read as South America's drip pointing at Antarctica.
issues.evidence:
Exact full-size frames:
- 610.40 (crop_610.40.jpg): orange rectangle with a straight edge at the left limb, cream cone, orange tip.
- 617.40 (crop_617.40.jpg): Gondwana with a large cream cone between the orange South America sliver and the Patagonian speck.
- 630.30: Cape Horn arrow starts from the speck.
- 642.20 (zip_strip.jpg): straight orange/cream cut across South America beside the zipper.
- 647.20: cream north-east Africa wedge with an orange Sinai speck.
- 674.00 (crop_674.00.jpg): paper figure with South America missing its cone and Africa notched.
Data: work_ch5a/member2.json has no coast_000 polygons 126, 50, 832, 341, 340 or 52 (the cone, 22-47°S) and none of 640, 623 or 453 (north-east Africa and Horn). classify.py's 0.3° rigid-fit test rejected them because they are separate GPlates plates. So they are drawn as SAND base land, and shot N does not draw them before the lock (BASE180 only appears at together+0.05).
issues.fix:
In /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/work_ch5a/member2.json:
- Append [126, 50, 832, 341, 340, 52] to "samerica".
- Append [640, 623, 453] to "africa".

In work_ch5a/export.py:
- Build a second cKDTree from only these added polygons.
- Add a coast_TTT polygon j to EXCL[T] when np.median(d) < np.radians(1.5) against that tree. The existing 0.06° test would miss them because they are not rigid with the track rotation, which would leave sand ghosts.

Re-run export.py to regenerate engine/www/ep/ep01/ch5a_data.js, then re-render ch5a (604.37-694.13). No ch5a.js change is needed: P.main stays the largest ring, so SEAMS.satl and the other contact seams are unchanged, and shot N's pieces then include the cone and north-east Africa.

issues.segment: s076 "Then the {m:zip}South Atlantic unzips from the bottom up"
issues.problem: The zipper-pull icon that should start the unzip at {m:zip} ("South", 640.45) first appears at about 642.2. That is about 1.75 s late against the marker and about 1 s after "unzips" (641.25). From the cut at 639.75 until 642.1 only static zipper teeth are on screen while the narration says the ocean is unzipping.
issues.evidence: Full-resolution crops (z/zip_strip.jpg, x 550-1050, y 300-1000): no slider at 641.80 or 642.00; the slider appears at the south end of the seam at 642.20 and is still there at 642.35. The counter reads 144 at 641.6 and about 142 at 642.2. The render log has T_OPEN0 146.25 and T_SNAP 112.75. drawZipper only shows the slider once k>0, meaning pair 0 at the south end is open, and that happens at T≈142. Tfwd puts M.zip at max(145, T_OPEN0+1) = 147.25.
issues.fix:
In ch5a.js:
- In the T_SNAP scan loop (line 114), also record the first T at which pair 0 opens: `if (T_FIRST == null && st.open[0] > 0.5) T_FIRST = T;`, declared next to T_OPEN0.
- In Tfwd (line 119), replace `[M.zip, Math.max(145, T_OPEN0 + 1)]` with `[M.zip + 0.15, T_FIRST ?? 142]`. That value is about 142, which stays between 148 at tG and 139 at M.split, so the keys remain monotonic.

The pull then pops at the south end at about 640.6 and climbs north under the words.
issues.module: ch5a (shot G, Tfwd keys / T_SNAP scan loop)

issues.problem: The cabin's left half hovers above the globe's curved limb: there is a dark, starry gap under its bottom-left corner, so the house looks like it floats in space next to the Explorer.
issues.evidence: 656.80 full-resolution crop (g/crop_656.80.jpg): the cabin's bottom-left corner is at about (570, 680) with stars visible below it, while the globe limb at that x is at about y=725. The gap is roughly 20-45 px along the left half of the cabin's base.
issues.fix: In ch5a.js shot J, change `CAB = { x: -0.6, y: -0.07, z: -0.55, ry: 0.42, rz: 0.11, s: 0.5 }` to y: -0.15 and rz: 0.2. The extra tilt follows the limb's curvature. Alternatively use x: -0.48 so the cabin sits nearer the top of the limb. Check with a still at 656.8 that the corner touches the limb.

issues.segment: s073-s074 "They lock together into one supercontinent: Gondwana" / keypiece / drip arrows
issues.problem: After the lock clunk the pieces still don't touch. Dark ocean channels separate Antarctica from India (the widest gap), Australia and the Patagonian tip; these are present-day coastline-fit gaps. So "lock together" and "at its heart" land on what reads as an archipelago around Antarctica.
issues.evidence: Exact frames 617.40 (crop_617.40.jpg), 620.20, 622.10 and 630.30: India-Antarctica gap about 60-80 px at full resolution, plus clear dark channels at Australia and the South America tip. Explode is 0 here (exAsm goes to 0 at gond-0.04, and shot C has no lift outside 621.26-622.03), so the gap is the data itself.
issues.fix:
In ch5a_paleo.js, Paleo.draw:
- Accept `o.shelf` (px).
- In the tracked-plate loop, stroke the path in the fill colour with lineWidth = o.shelf*sc before g.fill.
- Widen the white outline to 5.2*sc + o.shelf*sc so it stays outside.
- Do the same for the Antarctica polygons in drawBase, adding shelf to baseKey.

In ch5a.js, pass shelf: 12 in the po object of shot A (only while t > M.gond - 0.2), shot C and shot E. This visually closes the 0.5-1° coastline-fit gaps.
